Control green, and three of my own mutations all RED: M1 restores the exact pre-fix envelope (dirty moved back inside content repo_rev) -> RED; M2 leaks the same dirt-derived fact under a DIFFERENT key name (tree_state: pristine/soiled) -> RED, so the test is not keyed to the literal token dirty; M3 puts any per-invocation varying field in content (a nonce) -> RED, so it catches content divergence generally rather than one special case. The test also establishes its own premise rather than assuming it (asserts clean porcelain is empty and dirty porcelain is not, and asserts the declared rows and the commit are identical) before its headline assertion. r4-quality.title: Quality vs inherited rules
r4-quality.imperative: Does the change meet the inherited project/section rules (the handoff's constraints)? Append a check per rule. Record pass/fail with a finding.
r4-quality.finding: THE DOCSTRING ARGUMENT IS SOUND - I stressed it rather than read it. The claim is that content does not need dirty for honesty because the per-file blob OID already answers which-bytes-did-this-agent-get. Attack: could a reader be misled by repo_rev {commit: X} with no dirty marker into thinking git checkout X reproduces what was delivered? That inference is blocked, and MORE strongly than the docstring claims: the manifest is SELF-CHECKING - for any declared repo-rooted path you can compare the row rev against git rev-parse X:path, so per-declared-file dirtiness is DERIVABLE from content alone. The flag was not merely coarser than the OID, it was redundant with respect to the declared files, and the only extra information it carried was about files OUTSIDE the manifest scope - undeclared ones - which is precisely why it broke determinism. That is a sharper formulation of the same conclusion and I offer it as a suggestion, not a defect. No hole found: the derivation covers only repo-rooted paths tracked at X, but commit never claimed to describe skill-rooted or out-of-repo files, so that is a scope the stamp never asserted, not a gap. Nothing was lost by the move - run.dirty still records it for a human. RULING ON SCOPING run.dirty: honest as-is, do NOT scope it. In /run the field is documented as a fact about the producing environment, which is exactly what a repo-wide git status --porcelain answers, so the name and the mechanism agree; repo-wide is what Tommy asked for; and a declaration-scoped dirty would duplicate what the per-file OIDs already make derivable while re-creating the temptation to move it back into content. One optional nit only: the JSON key is a bare dirty sitting beside roots/host, so a reader could take it as the declared files are dirty - repo_dirty or worktree_dirty would remove that ambiguity at zero cost. MAJOR-2 CLOSED, and better than I asked. The guard comment now states exactly what it pins and explicitly disclaims what it does not (it does NOT mean build_manifest never shells out; the indirection keeps the guard literally true, not a claim that assembly is subprocess-free). And the new test_build_manifest_with_both_edges_injected_shells_out_to_nothing pins the invariant that actually matters, patching subprocess.run/Popen at module level rather than merely asserting the fakes were used. I verified its trap is ARMED: with subprocess trapped, the DEFAULT path raises (proving the default really does shell out, so the comment is honest) while both-edges-injected performs zero calls (proving the guarantee).

triage_candidates.statement: the poison framework has a latent trap: shadowing default_repo_state by appending source does NOT reach build_manifest, because it is bound as a default argument at def time. The shipped POISONS (encode, content) are call-time lookups so they work, but a future repo_state poison would silently no-op and read as green. Worth a comment beside POISONS.

un-gitignoring .agent-work/ will make repo_rev.dirty permanently true and so useless: verified a file under gitignored .agent-work reads dirty=False today, and every run writes there (the manifest itself lands there). Changes what dirty MEANS, not just where the manifest is stored.

optional nit: the /run key is a bare `dirty` sitting beside roots/host, so a JSON reader could take it as "the declared files are dirty" rather than "the producing worktree was dirty"; repo_dirty or worktree_dirty removes the ambiguity at zero cost

boundary, NOT a defect and not the dirty class: a plain copy with no .git delivering byte-identical declared canon yields repo_rev {commit: null} while a real checkout yields the SHA, so content differs. Outside the determinism claim scope, which says "checkout" - and the docstring is precisely worded on exactly this ("identical in any checkout of that commit, anywhere").
